source.quote: On October 14, 2026, we notified developers using certain GPT-4 series models of their deprecation and removal from the API on January 14, 2027.

The pinned model string "gpt-4o-2024-08-06" must be replaced with a supported model, gpt-6-luna per the notice.

## GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini, GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1 mini snapshots shut down Jan 14, 2027; migrate to gpt-6-luna [Needs review]

### Change

Changed the model in functions/src/index.ts from gpt-4o-2024-08-06 to gpt-6-luna. Added functions/model.check.js, which asserts the new model name and that no gpt-4 id remains.

Files touched:
- `functions/model.check.js`
- `functions/src/index.ts`
- `tsconfig.app.tsbuildinfo`
- `tsconfig.node.tsbuildinfo`

### Why

gpt-4o-2024-08-06 shuts down on 2027-01-14. OpenAI's recommended replacement is gpt-6-luna, which supports chat.completions.

> On October 14, 2026, we notified developers using certain GPT-4 series models of their deprecation and removal from the API on January 14, 2027.

Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck | pass | pass | 0 |
| build | pass | pass | 0 |
| model-check | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- model-check, added by the agent: `export VITE_FIREBASE_API_KEY='placeholder' VITE_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN='placeholder.firebaseapp.com' VITE_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID='placeholder' VITE_FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET='placeholder.appspot.com' VITE_FIREBASE_MESSAGING_SENDER_ID='000000000000' VITE_FIREBASE_APP_ID='placeholder' VITE_OPENAI_API_KEY='placeholder'; node functions/model.check.js` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider tool calls recorded by the harness:
- `openai__openai_model_lookup`: pass
- `openai__openai_check_request`: pass

The agent's validator claims (not proof; graded against the recorded calls):
- openai_model_lookup: pass (gpt-6-luna is active and supports chat/completions)
- openai_check_request: pass (No unknown or deprecated params)

Prepared before the baseline:
- Checks ran with placeholder env: VITE_FIREBASE_API_KEY, VITE_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN, VITE_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID, VITE_FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET, VITE_FIREBASE_MESSAGING_SENDER_ID, VITE_FIREBASE_APP_ID, VITE_OPENAI_API_KEY.

Test of this change: `model-check`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- Whether gpt-6-luna's output works with the SDK's beta.chat.completions.parse and zodResponseFormat (openai@4.77.3) was not checked. The SDK was not upgraded.
- Extraction quality on real resumes was not compared with gpt-4o.

### Behaviour changes

- The extraction model changes from gpt-4o to gpt-6-luna, so output quality, latency and cost may differ.
- gpt-6-luna is a reasoning model. The request sends no sampling params, so none had to be dropped.

---

## Result
Files changed: functions/model.check.js, functions/src/index.ts, tsconfig.app.tsbuildinfo, tsconfig.node.tsbuildinfo
Verdict: migrated. Changed the model in functions/src/index.ts from gpt-4o-2024-08-06 to gpt-6-luna. Added functions/model.check.js, which asserts the new model name and that no gpt-4 id remains.

preparation.reasoning: The root project is a plain Vite/React/TypeScript app with no codegen or prepare/postinstall steps, so no setup commands are needed. The functions/ folder is a separate project, and the root checks (tsc --noEmit, yarn build via tsc -b and vite build) don't run there, so installing its dependencies isn't needed. The README says a .env file is required, so I'm supplying placeholder Vite env vars (Firebase and OpenAI keys) in case the code reads them at load or build time. The names are guessed from the README and typical setup, not confirmed against the code, and none are real secrets.

review.summary: The one call site in functions/src/index.ts (line ~51, beta.chat.completions.parse) now uses "gpt-6-luna" instead of "gpt-4o-2024-08-06". That covers the only model string the match agent named. The zodResponseFormat call at line 60 has no model parameter and needs no change. Three things weaken the PR. The new model-check script only does a string match on the source. Nothing shows that gpt-6-luna accepts structured outputs (json_schema response_format) through the beta parse helper, or that the repo's pinned openai SDK version handles it. The PR also commits two unrelated generated tsbuildinfo files at the repo root. The needs-review grade is appropriate: typecheck and build passing prove nothing about the model ID, because `model` accepts any string, and no live call was made.

concerns.issue: I could not confirm that "gpt-6-luna" is a valid model ID that supports Structured Outputs with response_format json_schema (zodResponseFormat). The quoted deprecation notice names the retirement but this review cannot confirm the replacement's capabilities. Check the deprecations page and the model docs. If the model lacks strict json_schema support, parse() will throw at runtime, the catch block will hide it as a generic 'internal' error, and every resume extraction will fail.

The change may alter behaviour beyond the swap. A newer or reasoning-class model can have different latency, cost, and output tendencies. Examples: how it fills the required string fields (email, phone, education) when they are missing, given the prompt asks for null or an empty string while the schema requires strings. It may also reject parameters or have different defaults. None of this is exercised by the checks.

The check is a static string test: it confirms the literal 'model: "gpt-6-luna"' is present and that no 'gpt-4' appears. It proves the edit was made, not that the call works. It is also brittle: any future comment or string containing 'gpt-4' would fail it. Consider whether this file belongs in the repo at all, since it isn't wired into package.json scripts in the diff.

An unrelated TypeScript incremental build artifact was committed at the repo root, along with tsconfig.node.tsbuildinfo. These are generated by the build check and should be removed from the PR or added to .gitignore.

The diff does not show which openai SDK version is pinned. openai.beta.chat.completions.parse and openai/helpers/zod exist in the 4.x line, but newer SDKs moved parse out of beta. Confirm that the installed version accepts the new model and has no client-side model allowlist or typing issue. Typecheck passing suggests it is fine, but the model param is typed loosely.

checkFirst: Confirm in the OpenAI deprecations and models docs that gpt-6-luna is the recommended replacement and supports Structured Outputs (json_schema strict) on Chat Completions.
Run one live call of extractStructuredData against a sample resume with the new model, using a Firebase emulator with OPENAI_API_KEY, and verify that `parsed` comes back populated.
Drop tsconfig.app.tsbuildinfo and tsconfig.node.tsbuildinfo from the PR, and decide whether functions/model.check.js should be kept.

source.quote: * require Node.js 22 and codify version support ([#2026](https://github.com/openai/openai-node/issues/2026))

tasks.reasoning: The repo pins openai (npm) 4.77.3, which falls in the '<7.0.0' range. 7.0.0 requires Node.js 22, so upgrading means the Firebase Functions runtime (engines.node in functions/package.json and the deploy runtime) must also run Node 22. Nothing breaks today without an upgrade. The model retirement above may be fixable by just changing the model string on 4.77.3. The migration agent should check: whether staying on 4.x works with the replacement model; the functions Node runtime version; whether beta.chat.completions.parse still exists or moved to chat.completions.parse; and zodResponseFormat compatibility with the installed zod version. The 2026-07-27 date is the release date, not a shutdown cutoff, so this ranks below the model retirement despite the earlier date. The 7.43/7.44 Live Decisions type changes do not touch this repo and are not bundled here.

callSites.why: Uses beta.chat.completions.parse from openai 4.77.3. Moving to 7.x crosses several majors. Structured-output parse moved out of beta in later majors, so the call path may need updating.
zodResponseFormat (openai/helpers/zod) is imported from the SDK. Its import path and zod compatibility should be re-verified on 7.x.

## openai (npm) 7.0.0 requires Node.js 22 [Needs review]

### Change

In functions/: openai ^4.77.3 -> ^7.0.0 (resolved 7.48.0) and zod ^3.24.1 -> ^3.25.0 via yarn@1; engines.node 18 -> 22; openai.beta.chat.completions.parse -> openai.chat.completions.parse. Added functions/test/parse.check.js, which mocks fetch and checks the parse call and zodResponseFormat. The functions typecheck and the root checks pass.

Files touched:
- `functions/package.json`
- `functions/src/index.ts`
- `functions/test/parse.check.js`
- `functions/yarn.lock`
- `tsconfig.app.tsbuildinfo`
- `tsconfig.node.tsbuildinfo`

### Why

openai 7.x requires Node.js 22, so the Firebase Functions runtime has to move to Node 22. Crossing v5 removed the `beta.chat` namespace. openai 7's zod helper imports `zod/v4`, which zod 3.24.1 doesn't export, so zod had to be bumped too.

> * require Node.js 22 and codify version support ([#2026](https://github.com/openai/openai-node/issues/2026))

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/openai-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck | pass | pass | 0 |
| build | pass | pass | 0 |
| openai-v7-parse | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- openai-v7-parse, added by the agent: `export VITE_FIREBASE_API_KEY='placeholder' VITE_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN='placeholder.firebaseapp.com' VITE_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID='placeholder' VITE_FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET='placeholder.appspot.com' VITE_FIREBASE_MESSAGING_SENDER_ID='placeholder' VITE_FIREBASE_APP_ID='placeholder' VITE_OPENAI_API_KEY='placeholder'; cd functions && node test/parse.check.js` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider tool calls recorded by the harness:
- `openai__openai_model_lookup`: fail
- `openai__package_lookup`: pass
- `openai__openai_check_request`: pass

concerns.issue: `ResumeExtractionSchema` has four `.optional()` fields without `.nullable()`: address, aboutMe, yearsOfExperience and jobRole-adjacent fields such as address/aboutMe/yearsOfExperience. Newer openai-node `zodResponseFormat` and strict structured outputs treat optional-without-nullable differently; some versions throw or warn at schema build time, or the API rejects it. `parse.check.js` only tests `z.object({a: z.string()})`, so this path is unproven. Run the check with the real schema, or confirm the v7 helper's behaviour in `openai/helpers/zod` and the CHANGELOG.
